expectations.text: Separates what goes to the authors, to the editor, and what is kept private
expectations.evidence: Section 3 explicitly splits To the authors / To the editor / Keep private.

expectations.text: Frames reuse/attribution/validation of established methods as the governing thesis for an integrated-platform paper (not a bug hunt)
expectations.evidence: Section 1 states reuse/attribution/validation + reproducibility is the governing thesis for an integrated platform, not a bug hunt.

expectations.text: Preserves confidentiality: warns against opening GitHub issues / contacting authors via the repo, and flags the journal AI-in-review policy
expectations.evidence: Section 6 warns 'Do NOT open GitHub issues', preserve anonymity, and check the journal AI-use policy (Section 0).

expectations.text: Applies the 'reviewer is not the authors' QA' framing (bugs as evidence for the thesis, not a debugging service)
expectations.evidence: Section 1/2 state the install failure etc. are reproducibility evidence and 'not something you should resolve by debugging their scripts'.

expectations.text: Handles COI correctly: names the class of DEA tools and does not cite the reviewer's own package in the submittable text
expectations.evidence: Flagged the COI up front and named the class, BUT the drafted review_for_authors.txt lists 'prolfqua' inside the DEA class in the SUBMITTED text (prolfqua count=1) - the reviewer's own package should not be cited in the submitted review at all.

expectations.text: Recommends a concise, thesis-first, human-voiced review (~750 words) rather than a five-page audit
expectations.evidence: Recommends thesis-first, ~750-word review; its own drafted review is 759 words.
